_disclaimer: Default values are calibrated against a reference bugfest environment. See ADR-0013 (Module configuration management) for the governance model behind this file. Kong is not a JVM application, so there is no java section. Resource values and nginx tuning must be adjusted to the target host capacity.

resources.name: cpu
resources.description: CPU request/limit for the kong container

resources.name: memory
resources.description: Memory hard limit for the kong container in MiB; must cover KONG_MEM_CACHE_SIZE, which is allocated twice by Kong, plus the nginx worker processes

resources.name: memoryReservation
resources.description: Memory reservation (soft limit) for the kong container in MiB

deployment.description: Kong runs in database mode, so all replicas share the routes, services and plugins stored in PostgreSQL. On every start the entrypoint bootstraps and applies Kong migrations and then runs deck sync for the tagged FOLIO configuration, both of which are idempotent. Because it also runs kong migrations finish, replicas of different Kong versions should not run side by side during an upgrade.

EnvVars.name: KONG_DATABASE
EnvVars.description: Datastore used by Kong. FOLIO relies on database mode (postgres): modules register their services and routes through the Admin API and the entrypoint runs database migrations.

EnvVars.name: KONG_PG_HOST
EnvVars.description: Hostname of the PostgreSQL server holding the Kong database.

EnvVars.name: KONG_PG_PORT
EnvVars.description: TCP port of the PostgreSQL server.

EnvVars.name: KONG_PG_DATABASE
EnvVars.description: Name of the PostgreSQL database used by Kong.

EnvVars.name: KONG_PG_USER
EnvVars.description: PostgreSQL user for the Kong database (sourced from secret store). Needs rights to run schema migrations, which the entrypoint executes on every start.

EnvVars.name: KONG_PG_PASSWORD
EnvVars.description: PostgreSQL password for the Kong database user (sourced from secret store).

EnvVars.name: KONG_PROXY_LISTEN
EnvVars.description: Address and port on which Kong accepts proxy traffic from outside the platform (Stripes UI, external scripts). Setting a single plain-HTTP listener drops Kong's default 8443 TLS listener; TLS is expected to terminate in front of Kong.

EnvVars.name: KONG_ADMIN_LISTEN
EnvVars.description: Address and port of the Kong Admin API, used by mgr-tenants and mgr-tenant-entitlements to register services and routes and by the entrypoint for its readiness check. The Admin API has no authentication, so expose it only to the internal network.

EnvVars.name: KONG_ADMIN_GUI_API_URL
EnvVars.description: URL of the Admin API as reachable from the browser of a Kong Manager user; Kong Manager (port 8002) uses it to talk to the Admin API.

EnvVars.name: KONG_PLUGINS
EnvVars.description: Plugins Kong loads. The entrypoint appends the FOLIO auth-headers-manager plugin to this value, so it must be set (bundled loads all plugins shipped with Kong).

EnvVars.name: KONG_ROUTER_FLAVOR
EnvVars.description: Router implementation. The CORS and version routes in the FOLIO declarative configuration are written as expressions, so this must stay expressions. Baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: DECK_SERVICE_PROTOCOL
EnvVars.description: Protocol used by the CORS and version services that deck creates for Kong's own endpoints; substituted into the declarative configuration. Baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: CORS_ORIGINS
EnvVars.description: Space-separated list of origins (URLs or PCRE regexes) allowed by the Kong CORS plugin. When unset, all origins (*) are allowed; set it in production. A single plain URL is not enforced by Kong 3.9, so use an anchored regex such as ^https://folio\.example\.com$ or list two origins.

EnvVars.name: KONG_HEADERS
EnvVars.description: Kong-generated response headers (Server, Via, latency tokens). off suppresses them so the Kong version is not disclosed. Baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_LOCATION_PROXY_SET_HEADER
EnvVars.description: nginx proxy_set_header injected into the proxy location to strip the Priority request header, a workaround for the DoS vulnerability CVE-2025-31650. Do not remove. Baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: KONG_LOG_LEVEL
EnvVars.description: Log level of the Kong/nginx error log (debug, info, notice, warn, error, crit, alert, emerg).

EnvVars.name: KONG_PROXY_ACCESS_LOG
EnvVars.description: Destination and format name of the proxy access log. The txns format is defined by KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LOG_FORMAT. Baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: KONG_ADMIN_ACCESS_LOG
EnvVars.description: Destination and format name of the Admin API access log; it shares stdout with the proxy access log. Baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LOG_FORMAT
EnvVars.description: Definition of the txns access log format, including the request ID and the tenant from the x-okapi-tenant header. Overrides the format baked into the image.

EnvVars.name: KONG_MEM_CACHE_SIZE
EnvVars.description: Size of each of the two shared-memory caches Kong uses for database entities (kong_core_cache and kong_cache), so total usage is twice this value. Raise it when many routes and services are registered; size the container memory accordingly.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_WORKER_PROCESSES
EnvVars.description: Number of nginx worker processes. Kong's default is auto (one per CPU core of the host); a fixed number is used so a container sharing a large host does not start excess workers.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE
EnvVars.description: Maximum allowed size of a client request body. Must be large enough for the biggest file uploaded through the gateway, such as data import files.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_CLIENT_HEADER_BUFFER_SIZE
EnvVars.description: Buffer size for reading the client request headers in the http block.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_PROXY_CLIENT_HEADER_BUFFER_SIZE
EnvVars.description: Buffer size for reading the client request headers in the proxy server block.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LARGE_CLIENT_HEADER_BUFFERS
EnvVars.description: Number and size of buffers for large client request headers in the http block. Required because requests carry large headers, such as JWT-bearing cookies; requests with headers above the total are rejected with 400.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_PROXY_LARGE_CLIENT_HEADER_BUFFERS
EnvVars.description: Number and size of buffers for large client request headers in the proxy server block. Keep it equal to KONG_NGINX_HTTP_LARGE_CLIENT_HEADER_BUFFERS.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_PROXY_PROXY_BUFFERS
EnvVars.description: Number and size of buffers used to read the upstream response in the proxy server block.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_PROXY_PROXY_BUFFER_SIZE
EnvVars.description: Size of the buffer holding the first part of the upstream response (the headers); must be at least as large as the biggest response header set returned by modules.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_HTTP_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT
EnvVars.description: nginx keepalive_timeout for client connections. A bare number is seconds, so 600000 keeps an idle client connection open for about 7 days; use a value such as 600 or 600s for ten minutes.

EnvVars.name: KONG_NGINX_UPSTREAM_KEEPALIVE
EnvVars.description: nginx keepalive directive injected into the Kong upstream block: the maximum number of idle upstream connections cached per worker process. It is a connection count, not a time.

EnvVars.name: KONG_UPSTREAM_KEEPALIVE_IDLE_TIMEOUT
EnvVars.description: Seconds an idle upstream keepalive connection stays open before it is closed (Kong default 60); 0 keeps idle connections open indefinitely.
